fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into Order Confirmations
fields.features_subheading: Order confirmation automation sends the customer's confirmation when an order is paid and checks the supplier's reply to each PO.
fields.feature_1:
Each paid order, picked up from your store

The app connects to your store or order system through its API and picks up each order once it is paid. The order and every email sent for it land in a database you own.
fields.feature_2:
One confirmation, split by shipment

When an order holds items with different ship dates, the email lists each shipment with its own date. The customer sees what leaves first and what follows, before writing to ask.
fields.feature_3:
Supplier PDFs read into fields

The app reads a supplier's confirmation PDF into fields with AI: PO number, lines, quantities, prices, and dates. A value it cannot read with confidence goes to a person to check.
fields.feature_4:
Tolerances you set for price and date

You decide how far a confirmed price or delivery date may move from the PO before a buyer looks. Lines inside your limits are accepted, and the rest wait for a decision.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders first, then the buyer hears

A PO with no confirmation gets an email reminder to the supplier at the hour you pick. If the supplier stays quiet, the buyer gets an alert, and no task cap limits how many run.
fields.feature_6:
The full code, in your GitHub

Export the app's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. Anyone on the team can read the exact rule behind each email sent and each PO line flagged, and change it.

fields.usecase_heading: Confirmations Going Out and Coming In
fields.tab_content_1:
Candles in 2 days, the diffuser on November 18

Wren Halloway orders 3 Juniper candles at $24 each and a preorder diffuser at $38 from Brambleton Candle Co., $110 in all. When payment clears on order #20417, the app emails her a confirmation with two shipments. The candles ship within 2 business days, and the diffuser ships on November 18.
fields.tab_content_2:
Order #8812 moves address and keeps its total

Fallowmere Coffee keeps an order open to edits for 60 minutes after checkout. Odessa Pruitt changes the ship-to address on order #8812 after 25 minutes. The app sends her a confirmation marked Updated that shows the old address and the new one, and the $41.50 total stays the same.
fields.tab_content_3:
Harnet raised the hinge price to $3.35

Kestrelwood Cabinets sends PO-4471 to Harnet Hardware for 400 soft-close hinges at $3.10 each. Harnet's confirmation PDF says $3.35 a hinge, and the app reads it into fields and marks the price line as changed. The buyer, Tobiah Ferrante, sees a $100 difference across 400 hinges to accept or dispute.
fields.tab_content_4:
PO-1186 sits unconfirmed, and the buyer hears at 72 hours

Lindqvist Dental Lab sends PO-1186 to Corvane Ceramics for delivery on November 4. With no confirmation after 48 hours, the app emails Corvane a reminder. At 72 hours, the buyer, Marisol Achterberg, gets a direct message about PO-1186, due November 4.

fields.howto_title: How to Build Order Confirmation Automation
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan order confirmation automation for customers and suppliers, then build and test it in Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide when the email goes out
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Write a tolerance for supplier changes
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the fields a customer confirmation carries: the order number, each item with its price, the total, the ship-to address, and a date for each shipment. Add a line on how to change or cancel the order, because that is the first thing customers ask.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Send the customer confirmation when payment clears, not when the cart is submitted. A declined card then never gets one. If you take preorders, decide whether one email lists every shipment or each shipment gets its own email.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick how long a customer can change an order after checkout, and which changes you accept, such as a new address or a different size. Each accepted change sends a new confirmation, and you decide what the updated email shows next to the original value.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For each field on a supplier confirmation, write the change you accept without review. A delivery date one day late might pass on its own, while any price change waits for the buyer named on the PO.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Pick when to chase a supplier
fields.howto_step_5_des: Pick the hour after a PO goes out when the supplier gets a reminder, and the hour when the buyer hears instead. Use the supplier contact on the PO and name one buyer per PO. Each alert then reaches one person.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Paste your fields, timings, and tolerances into one prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the emails, the PO checks, and the database behind them, connected to your store through its API, and you change any rule later by asking for it.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Run 5 orders through before launch: a paid order, a preorder, an edited address, a PO confirmed at a changed price, and a PO never confirmed. Check that each email and each alert reaches the person you expect.
fields.hero_prompt: Build order confirmation automation that runs on its own and logs every step.

faq_plan.a: Order confirmation automation sends or checks order confirmations without anyone typing them. On the selling side, the app emails each customer the order details once payment clears. On the buying side, it reads the confirmation a supplier sends back for a purchase order and compares every line with the PO.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up order confirmation automation?
faq_plan.a: Write down what each confirmation shows and when it goes out, then describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder. Emergent builds the emails and the supplier checks, with your orders in a database you own. Connect your store and the inbox that receives supplier replies, then run a few real orders through before anyone outside sees it.

faq_plan.q: What should order confirmation automation put in the customer email?
faq_plan.a: Put in the order number, what was bought and for how much, where it ships, and when. Add a link for edits and cancellations and a reply address that reaches a person. In an app built with Emergent, every one of those values comes from the order record in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should order confirmation automation send an email when an order is canceled?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A cancellation confirmation names the order, the items canceled, and the refund amount and method, and the customer no longer has to rely on the original email. An item sent back after delivery is a separate flow, and returns automation covers its label and refund.

faq_plan.q: Can order confirmation automation add product recommendations to the email?
faq_plan.a: It can, with care. The FTC's CAN-SPAM guide says an email's primary purpose is transactional if it consists only of content such as confirming a commercial transaction the recipient already has agreed to. It adds that the law views these categories narrowly. When an email contains both kinds of content, the primary purpose of the message is the deciding factor.

faq_plan.q: Does order confirmation automation work with purchase order acknowledgments?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A purchase order acknowledgment is the supplier's reply to a PO, and X12 defines an EDI version, the 855 Purchase Order Acknowledgment, for a seller's acknowledgment of a buyer's purchase order. Whether the reply arrives as an 855 or as a PDF by email, the app reads it and checks each line against the PO.

faq_plan.q: Should order confirmation automation include a tracking number?
faq_plan.a: Only if the order has already shipped. A confirmation goes out when the order is paid, before a label exists. It carries the expected ship date instead. The tracking number belongs in the shipping notice sent when the label prints, a separate email that shipping automation sends on its own trigger.

faq_plan.q: Can order confirmation automation handle orders from more than one store?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as each store has an API the app can connect to. The app picks up paid orders from each store, records which store each came from, and sends each confirmation with that store's name and reply address. Emergent sets no task cap, and a busy sale day runs on the same rules.

faq_plan.q: How fast should order confirmation automation send the customer email?
faq_plan.a: Send it on the payment event itself, not on an hourly or nightly schedule. A confirmation that waits for a batch leaves the customer wondering whether the order went through. In the app Emergent builds, each paid order triggers its own email, and the send time is saved with the order.

faq_plan.q: Does order confirmation automation replace purchase approvals?
faq_plan.a: No. It starts once a PO has gone out: it reads the supplier's reply, checks it against the PO, and chases suppliers who never confirm. Approvals and buying policy come earlier, before a PO exists, and belong to procurement automation.

plan.angle: The top 10 splits in two: five results (Doxis, Docbits, free-com, easy software, Onventis) mean the confirmation a supplier sends back on a purchase order, matched against the PO, and the rest (Omnisend, a UiPath forum thread, Pabbly videos) mean the confirmation email a store sends a customer after checkout. No result shows both. This page shows both directions as one app: the customer email that goes out on payment and splits a preorder onto its own ship date, the updated confirmation after a customer edits an order, a supplier confirmation read and checked line by line against the PO, and the chase when a supplier never confirms. Order intake and credit holds stay on the order processing page, labels and tracking on the shipping page, and purchasing policy on the procurement page.
